articles.body:
Florida would be in the 12-team College Football Playoff bracket for the first time based on The Associated Press Top 25 released Sunday and the Gators would host a first-round game.

First-year coach Jon Sumrall's team zoomed up 13 spots to No. 8 in the poll, which would give the Gators the last home-field spot and the Southeastern Conference a total of six teams in the field.

Texas, Georgia, Notre Dame and Miami would be the top four seeds and Ohio State, Indiana, Alabama and Florida would host first-round games.

The five highest-ranked conference champions — from the Power Four and one from the Group of Six — will qualify for the CFP. The other seven spots will be filled by the next highest-ranked teams. One of those at-large teams will be Notre Dame if the Fighting Irish are among the top 12 in the CFP's final rankings.

The Big Ten would have two teams in the field and the Big 12, Atlantic Coast Conference and Pac-12 would have one each. Notre Dame would be in as an independent, and Boise State would represent the Pac-12 as the top Group of Six champion.

Based on the AP rankings, the CFP would open like this:

No. 9 seed Mississippi at No. 8 Florida. Winner vs. No. 1 Texas.

No. 12 seed Boise State at Ohio State. Winner vs. No. 4 Miami.

No. 10 seed BYU at No. 7 Alabama. Winner vs. No. 2 Georgia.

No. 11 seed LSU at No. 6 Indiana. Winner vs. No. 3 Notre Dame.

The first three teams outside the bracket: Texas Tech, Utah and Iowa.

The Red Raiders are ranked No. 12 by the AP but would get bumped by Boise State, the highest-ranked Group of Six team.

First-round games are Dec. 18 and 19, quarterfinals Dec. 30 and Jan. 1, semifinals Jan. 14 and 15 and the championship game is Jan. 25 at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas.

The AP will publish brackets based on the weekly Top 25 until the CFP selection committee unveils its initial rankings Nov. 3.

articles.title: £80m transfer target knows it’s “a big win” that Liverpool want him
articles.summary: Yankuba Minteh reportedly still wants a move to Liverpool.Gambian football expert Baboucarr Fallaboweh told Sport Witness that the Brighton & Hove Albion win...
articles.body:
Yankuba Minteh reportedly still wants a move to Liverpool .

Gambian football expert Baboucarr Fallaboweh told Sport Witness that the Brighton & Hove Albion winger will likely stay in the Premier League if he leaves the south coast-based outfit.

The former Feyenoord star continues to recover from injury, but is expected to return to action after the September international break .

Yankuba Minteh wants Liverpool to come back in for him

Interestingly, Fallaboweh suggested that the footballer's ongoing presence on the sidelines could complicate matters: "I think Liverpool. He will still want to go to Liverpool. Depending on [how] Liverpool will activate that desire to still have him.

"Because right now, his situation has not been helped because he is injured. If not, then you could have more justification for him to showcase his performance why Liverpool were after him."

"But at the overall situation, even if he moves, I don't think he will move outside the Premier League. Manchester United can come banging on their doors."

"It's a big win for him to be associated with Liverpool. So, it gives other big European clubs around the world to take a closer look at him now that they know Brighton 's actual price. So, it will be easier for them to explore it."

However, with player and club expecting a return in the near future, we don't necessarily see this as a dealbreaker if Liverpool are still keen on the attacker come January.

Certainly, it won't have escaped the notice of fans that the Reds were perfectly happy to come in for Minteh even while he was still firmly out injured during pre-season.

So, we can't imagine that we'll be put off from making a move down the line if we're still keen on shoring up the right flank. That said, Brighton will first have to be willing to lower their £80m asking price – or the 22-year-old's performances this term will have to justify the price tag!

The problem for Liverpool will be justifying the signing of another winger without one heading out the exit door. Between Cody Gakpo , Bradley Barcola , Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha , Liverpool technically have the numbers on the flanks. Of course, as we'd be quick to point out, we're still lacking a natural right-sided (ideally left-footed) wideman.

But would the club sanction the arrival of another winger at a time when we're still short in midfield and right-back? Certainly not without first selling a player, and the most obvious candidate in Gakpo is currently enjoying the season of his life at Anfield, so that's just not a goer.

If you ask us, Lamine Camara is surely the top candidate to seal a move to L4 in the next transfer window.

We just can't see Yankuba Minteh getting his move to Liverpool much before the summer, assuming Julian Ward and Co. haven't identified an alternative target by then.

articles.summary: Barcelona star Eric García has on Sunday evening been granted an immediate departure from the Spanish national team camp. This comes in a bid to ‘avoid any r...
articles.body:
Barcelona star Eric García has on Sunday evening been granted an immediate departure from the Spanish national team camp. This comes in a bid to 'avoid any risk' when it comes to the player's fitness.

Defender Eric for his part sparked concern back in Catalunya's capital on Saturday evening. Less than an hour out from world champions Spain locking horns with England in a Nations League clash, the former Manchester City man was scratched from Luis de la Fuente's matchday squad.

Whilst warming up with his teammates at Wembley, Eric pulled up with sudden pain in his left knee.

From here, the 25-year-old was put through a round of tests and scans by the Spanish medical team on Sunday afternoon. And as alluded to above, the results proved noteworthy enough for action to be taken.

As per a statement across La Roja's website and social media platforms, Eric has been replaced in the country's squad for the remainder of the internatonal break by Atlético Madrid's Robin Le Normand :

'Atletico Madrid player Robin Le Normand replaces Eric Garcia in the Spanish national team camp, which is playing in the UEFA Nations League group stage.

'The FC Barcelona center-back felt some discomfort in his left knee and after the tests carried out, it has been decided to withdraw him from the squad due to the proximity of the upcoming international matches, thus avoiding any risk and preserving the player's health.'

Eric will now return to base in Barcelona to undergo treatment.

articles.title: The surprising reason Cristiano Ronaldo paints his toenails black ahead of Portugal vs Norway clash
articles.summary: Discover the surprising reason behind Cristiano Ronaldo's black toenails ahead of the Portugal vs Norway match, exploring health and performance benefits for athletes.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo's latest pre-match picture caught people's attention for a reason that had nothing to do with football, as the Portugal superstar showed off his black toenails while preparing for the Nations League clash with Norway.The 41-year-old is expected to feature for Portugal on Sunday evening and posted a picture of himself wearing leg compression boots as part of his recovery routine. But with his bare feet also visible, it was the colour of Ronaldo's toenails that immediately stood out.Ronaldo has always been obsessive about what he does away from the pitch, with his training, recovery and general approach to looking after his body playing a huge part in his extraordinary longevity. Even his painted toenails, it turns out, have a practical reason behind them.So why does Cristiano Ronaldo paint his toenails black?Ronaldo's feet have taken plenty of punishment over the course of a career that has lasted more than two decades, but the black colour on his toenails is reportedly not simply the result of bruising or the wear and tear of playing football.The Athletic reported that Ronaldo paints his toenails black because the nail polish is believed to offer some protection against bacteria and fungal infections.That is particularly relevant for someone who trains and exercises almost every day and spends long periods wearing sweaty football boots and training shoes. Warm, damp conditions can make it easier for fungal infections to develop, which is why foot care becomes particularly important for athletes who spend so much time in footwear.Britain's Royal College of Podiatry has previously pointed to a small study suggesting that nail varnish could provide some protection, although good foot hygiene remains the most important way to prevent problems.Dr Helen Branthwaite, a spokesperson for the Royal College of Podiatry, told The Athletic: “With over 250,000 sweat glands in your feet, the average person will produce around half a pint of sweat per day in their feet.”She explained that most fungal toenail infections begin with a fungal skin infection, commonly known as athlete's foot, which can then spread to the toenail.“Virtually all fungal toenail infections come from fungal skin infections, commonly known as athlete’s foot, which then spreads to the nail,” Branthwaite said.“Leaving this skin infection untreated is the biggest risk factor for developing nail fungus.”So while the black toenails might look unusual when Ronaldo posts a picture from his recovery routine, there is reportedly more to them than simply making a statement.Ronaldo is not the only sports star doing itThe habit is not particularly unusual in combat sports, where athletes regularly deal with heavy training loads, sweaty footwear and repeated impact on their feet.Former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson is understood to have painted his nails during his career, while former UFC middleweight champion Israel Adesanya has also been seen with painted nails.Former UFC heavyweight champion Andrei Arlovski was another fighter who sported painted nails during his career.There are also specialist nail varnishes and treatments that market themselves as helping to inhibit fungal growth, although Branthwaite stressed that the simplest form of prevention is still “good foot hygiene”.Ronaldo is also a well-known fan of the UFC, the Ultimate Fighting Championship, and the practice has become particularly visible among professional fighters.That does not necessarily mean Ronaldo is copying the fighters, however, with the explanation given for his own routine being linked to protecting his toenails rather than simply following a trend.For a player who has built much of his career around tiny details, it is perhaps fitting that even something as small as his toenails has become part of his preparation.Ronaldo is still chasing the 1,000-goal markThe black toenails may have been the talking point in Ronaldo's latest picture, but there is a much bigger number he is still chasing on the pitch.The Portugal captain has scored 979 goals for club and country and is now targeting the extraordinary milestone of 1,000 career goals.He came agonisingly close to reaching 980 in Portugal's win over Wales, only for a VAR check to prevent the goal from counting and leave him on 979.Ronaldo is expected to lead Portugal's attack again against Norway, with the latest Nations League fixture another opportunity to continue what has become one of the most remarkable scoring records in football.At 41, the forward is still putting the same attention into recovery and preparation that has helped keep him playing at the highest level for so long.And if that means painting his toenails black before pulling on his boots, Ronaldo clearly has no problem articles.summary: Encarriló seis victorias, algo que nunca había logrado, en los primeros minutos ante una UD que dio demasiadas facilidades atrás
articles.body: Avance. Un intenso y eficaz Eibar no sólo doblegó en Ipurua a una Las Palmas que concedió demasiado atrás, aunque apretó mucho en la recta final, sino que encadena seis victorias por primera vez en el fútbol profesional de la mano de Jokin Aranbarri y se sitúa provisionalmente al frente de la clasificación. La UD, muy lastrada por las numerosas bajas en defensa y que encima perdió al final a Iñaki por una doble amarilla, sufre su segunda derrota seguida. Al descanso se llegó con ventaja armera, sobre todo fruto de su gran puesta en escena. Y es que a los diez minutos ya mandaba el equipo de Jokin Aranbarri tras los goles de Mada, con un derechazo desde la frontal tras recibir de Adus Ares que desvió Iñaki, y de Álvaro Rodríguez, con un disparo cruzado a pase de Ares. Pudo incluso ampliar diferencias el Eibar, Martón tuvo dos claras pero se topó primero con Álex Suárez y después con Caro, gran parada la suya, y finalmente Pezzolesi recortó diferencias al rematar en el segundo palo el buen centro de Iván Jaime. La segunda parte comenzó con un Eibar dominando más y buscando la sentencia y una UD que buscaba la igualada, la cual rondó en un remate de Manu Fuster, tras dejada de Jesé, que salió rozando el poste. Sin embargo lo que llegó fue el tercero de un Eibar que volvió a aprovechar cierta pasividad en la zaga visitante y Martón marcó a placer tras una cesión de Guruzeta en jugada iniciada por Magunazelaia. Intentó la UD meterse en el partido, Iván Jaime rondó el gol con un centro chut que se fue envenenando, y al final lo consiguió con el primer gol de Jefté, que recibió de Elías, se giró y marcó con un disparo raso. Sufrió un poco al final, pero el cuadro armero duerme como líder de LaLiga Hypermotion.

articles.title: Chelsea 1-0 Arsenal: Alyssa Thompson's strike secures victory at Stamford Bridge and ends Gunners' unbeaten run
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Chelsea beat Arsenal 1-0 at Stamford Bridge; Alyssa Thompson scored the only goal after firing in from close range; Arsenal hit the post twice but their unbeaten run, stretching back to October 2025, comes to an end
articles.body:
Arsenal failed to make their early dominance count after striking the post twice through Kim Little and Mariona Caldentey before Thompson broke the deadlock at Stamford Bridge.

Keira Walsh's strike from distance was initially well kept out by Anneke Borbe, but the goalkeeper was left helpless when Thompson pounced in the box to fire home the rebound in emphatic style.

The Gunners - who had drawn their last two WSL matches - improved in the second half, with Chloe Kelly's angled drive blocked and Alessia Russo's shot charged down, but the hosts saw out the closing stages for a third WSL win.

Their unbeaten streak in the WSL, stretching back to October 2025, came to an end with it. The Gunners had not tasted defeat in their last 20 games before their trip to west London.

Victory takes Chelsea to within two points of league leaders Manchester City at the top of the table, while Arsenal are already seven points adrift ahead of their meeting with the champions on October 4.

Slegers 'disappointed' but believes in her players despite struggles

Arsenal boss Renee Slegers speaking to Sky Sports :

"Very disappointed. We know it's a tough game, Chelsea away. I think we did well in the first half in the physical battle and dominated until their goal. We found it hard in the second half and it cost us more energy.

"[We will] work hard, reflect and go forward. I want to take everything away from the players because I think they're at their very best when they're light. There is so much quality in the squad."

On what isn't clicking for Arsenal currently: "It's a cocktail of things. It's everything. Technical and psychological. We're looking at it. I believe in these players. The goals and the points will come. I believe in them."

On the title race: "We have to earn the right to talk about this because we've lost too many points at the moment. Look at the next game and get the points."

articles.title: Andrea Medina stars for Man Utd, Liverpool win Merseyside derby and are Arsenal's title hopes over? - WSL talking points
articles.summary: The Sky Sports writers analyse all the big talking points from across the weekend's action; are Arsenal's title hopes over after London derby defeat to Chelsea? Andrea Medina puts in "virtuoso display" for Man Utd; Liverpool end Anfield hoodoo with Merseyside derby win
articles.body:
Are Arsenal's title chances over already?

It seems a touch early to definitely say whether or not Arsenal's title chances are over already, but their start has left a lot to be desired.

Four games in, they have scored only twice and one of those goals - in the 1-1 draw with Man Utd last weekend - wasn't scored until the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

And now their unbeaten run in the WSL, which started all the way back on October 12 last year, has been ended by Chelsea.

It leaves the Gunners seven points adrift of leaders Man City already.

Head coach Renee Slegers was asked about that topic after full-time at Stamford Bridge and she said she wanted to "take the pressure off" of her players.

"I believe in these players. The goals will come and the points will come as well," she said.

"We have to earn the right again to talk about this [the title race] because we've lost too many points."

With a trip to City up next on October 4, the week ahead feels like a crucial one in the north Londoners' season. Dan Long

Sky Sports ' Laura Hunter highlighted Andrea Medina in the lead-up to this game , posing the question as to whether the Spaniard could be Man Utd's trump card.

Based on her performance on Sunday, the answer is a resounding yes.

Medina was the standout player by some distance at Leigh Sports Village: she created the most chances (4), took the most touches in the opposition box (11), hit the crossbar and scored United's crucial second goal.

Speaking on Sky Sports+ , commentator Gary Taphouse called it "a virtuoso display". It came as no surprise when she was named Player of the Match.

As Eva Olid's side look to build momentum after starting with two defeats and a draw, the former Spain U23 international could be the keystone. Dan Long

Liverpool's 2-0 win against Merseyside rivals Everton was the perfect remedy for the club's curse at Anfield.

Heading into this game, the Reds had lost eight of their last nine outings in the stadium. Five of those had come against the Toffees.

It was an assured and confident performance throughout. After Beata Olsson's early opener, which settled the nerves, it was just a matter of when, not if, the second arrived.

Cornelia Kapocs delivered and secured all three points. Liverpool move ahead of Everton in the process of their solid start to the campaign continuing.

The fixture list is a relentless one, however, with a trip to Birmingham in the Women's League Cup fast approaching before an away clash against another foe in Manchester United.

Getting over the hump that is their form at Anfield will be a welcome boost in tackling those challenges. Liverpool can now move forward with confidence. Patrick Rowe

A confident and strong 4-0 win for Tottenham against Aston Villa now opens up the conversation about a potential title race for the club.

No team has scored more than Spurs. Fifteen goals in their opening four games with just two goals conceded.

They are two points off Manchester City at the top but their upcoming run of fixtures will confirm whether they can assume the role of outside contenders for top spot.

London City Lionesses, Chelsea and Arsenal are their next three opponents in the WSL. Emerge from that October fixture list unscathed and serious conversations may need to be had about their chances...

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter said that people may need to start paying attention to Spurs in the build-up to this game. The game against Villa was another warning. Patrick Rowe

Birmingham may still be waiting for their first WSL win of the season, but this was a display that shows it will not be far around the corner.

The Blues are playing in the top flight for the first time in four years but have started the season winless from their first four games.

Birmingham led twice against Palace on Sunday, yet somehow needed a late equaliser to rescue a 3-3 draw.

However, it was Birmingham who nearly nicked a winner as Chancelle Effa Effa had a stoppage-time chance to dramatically snatch victory.

That shot was one of 19 for the home side, who had more attempts, shots on target and touches in the opposition box than Palace.

But at the other end, they allowed 17 shots as two mistakes cost them two goals against Palace, as a goalkeeper howler let in the visitors' first while a slip gave Palace their third.

If Amy Merrick's side can tighten up at the back and continue to produce positive attacking displays like the one against Palace, then surely they can earn their first WSL win soon. Declan Olley
